findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O errors (file not found, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, _> and use ? to propagate the io::Error

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing into a Vec<String> with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty or malformed line causes panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .get(0).ok_or(...) or restructure with split_once to avoid indexed access

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() has two violations: unchecked indexing on parts[1] and unwrap on parse result
findings.failure_mode: line with missing second field or non-numeric value panics instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Use .get(1).ok_or(...), then handle parse failure with map_err or ? to return a typed ParseError

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 to u16 with no bounds checking
findings.failure_mode: values above 65535 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect data
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap_or_else(...)) or parse directly as u16 with ? error propagation

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() + indexed access is used instead of split_once for two-field comma-delimited data
findings.failure_mode: allocates intermediate Vec<String> for every line and enables unchecked indexing; also breaks if value contains a comma
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (name, value_str) directly, then trim and parse value_str

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect embedded inside the data-transform iterator chain
findings.failure_mode: side effect leaks into what should be a pure mapping step; makes the iteration non-deterministic in observable behavior and inseparable from I/O
findings.fix: Remove println! from the iterator chain. If logging is needed, push a loggable event from the shell after parsing completes

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing in a single function that returns Vec instead of Result
findings.failure_mode: no typed error surface; caller cannot distinguish I/O failure from parse failure; core logic is not unit-testable in isolation
findings.fix: Split into: 1) fn load_text(path: &str) -> Result<String, io::Error>, 2) fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>. Shell calls load_text then pipes into parse_records

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve or bounded capacity handling; Vec::with_capacity is not used
findings.failure_mode: unbounded growth from untrusted file size; allocation failure is unhandled; no upper bound on memory usage
findings.fix: Add try_reserve with a bounded capacity and handle AllocationError; or accept a max_lines parameter and pre-reserve

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() then as u16 — neither checked conversion (try_from) nor checked arithmetic is used for the width-cast
findings.failure_mode: values in [65536, u32::MAX] silently truncate; domain invariant (value is u16) is not enforced at parse boundary
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16: parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(...) or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) with None -> Err mapping

findings.problem: Record fields are pub, exposing internal representation and allowing callers to construct invalid values
findings.failure_mode: illegal states are representable — callers can set value outside u16 domain or name to empty/malicious strings
findings.fix: Make fields private with a public constructor that validates, or use a newtype for name if domain rules exist

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in load_sessions
no allocation audit (try_reserve, bounded capacity) for Vec<Record> output
no second-ring evidence (mutation tests, property tests) for parse_records
no command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo test, cargo clippy) was run or reported
no bounded-allocation handling (try_reserve) anywhere in the crate
residual_risk: This is a static review with no commands run. The crate has multiple BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, side effects in iterator chain, split+collect+index pattern instead of split_once, mixed I/O and pure logic, and no Result type. Even if all findings were fixed, behavioral tests and command-gated verification (cargo fmt, cargo test, cargo clippy) would be required before delivery.
